title: Angles of polygons
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:21Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, mat-angle-sum-polygons, covers only the interior angle sum (n - 2) × 180° and is pitched at Year 7, while this point also requires the exterior angle sum of 360° for convex polygons, which it does not teach.

draft.title: Angles of polygons
card: A polygon with \(n\) sides can be split into \(n - 2\) triangles by drawing diagonals from one vertex. Each triangle has angles adding to \(180^{\circ}\).
The interior angles add to \((n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}\). For a hexagon, \(n = 6\), so the sum is \(4 \times 180^{\circ} = 720^{\circ}\).
An exterior angle is formed by extending one side. The exterior angles of any convex polygon add to \(360^{\circ}\), whatever the number of sides.
In a regular polygon all angles are equal. Each exterior angle is \(360^{\circ} \div n\), and the interior angle is \(180^{\circ}\) minus the exterior angle.
draft.remember: Interior angles add to \((n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}\). Exterior angles add to \(360^{\circ}\).

a.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon?
a.why: A pentagon has \(n = 5\), so the sum is \(3 \times 180^{\circ} = 540^{\circ}\). Using \(4 \times 180^{\circ} = 720^{\circ}\) is the tempting mistake of subtracting only 1 instead of 2.
a.clue: A pentagon splits into three triangles.

b.q: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is \(24^{\circ}\). How many sides does the polygon have, and what is each interior angle?
b.why: The number of sides is \(360 \div 24 = 15\). Each interior angle is \(180^{\circ} - 24^{\circ} = 156^{\circ}\). Giving \(24^{\circ}\) as the interior angle confuses it with the exterior angle.
b.clue: Exterior angles add to a fixed total, shared equally.

wants.brief: A hexagon with diagonals drawn from one vertex, splitting it into four triangles, each labelled with its angle sum of 180 degrees.
wants.why: It shows why the sum uses n minus 2 triangles.
